title: Ephesians Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ephesians chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ephesians Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ephesians Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Ephesians 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: You were dead in trespasses and sins
We walked according to the course of this world
questions.correctAnswer: You were dead in trespasses and sins
questions.explanation: The phrase 'you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins' is found in Ephesians 2:1, making it the first statement in the chapter.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:2 say about the past behavior of the people?
options: They walked according to the course of this world
questions.correctAnswer: They walked according to the course of this world
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:2 states that 'ye walked according to the course of this world', describing the past behavior.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:3, what were the people fulfilling?
options: The desires of the flesh and of the mind
questions.correctAnswer: The desires of the flesh and of the mind
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:3 mentions that they were 'fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind'.

questions.question: What is God described as in Ephesians 2:4?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4 states that 'God, who is rich in mercy', highlighting His nature.

questions.question: What has God done for us according to Ephesians 2:5?
options: Hath quickened us together with Christ
Sent us to preach the Gospel
questions.correctAnswer: Hath quickened us together with Christ
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:5 indicates that 'hath quickened us together with Christ', which is a central action described.

questions.question: In Ephesians 2:6, where are we made to sit?
options: In heavenly places in Christ Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: In heavenly places in Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:6 states that we are 'made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus'.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:7 say God will show in the ages to come?
options: The exceeding riches of his grace
questions.correctAnswer: The exceeding riches of his grace
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:7 mentions that 'he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace' in the ages to come.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:8, how are we saved?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8 clearly states that 'For by grace are ye saved through faith'.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:5 indicate about our state before being quickened?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:5 indicates that 'Even when we were dead in sins' describes our prior condition.

questions.question: Who works in the children of disobedience according to Ephesians 2:2?
options: The prince of the power of the air
questions.correctAnswer: The prince of the power of the air
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:2 states that they walked according to 'the prince of the power of the air'.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:3 say we were by nature?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:3 states that we 'were by nature the children of wrath'.

questions.question: True or False: God loved us with a great love according to Ephesians 2:4.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4 states 'for his great love wherewith he loved us', confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: We are saved by our own works according to Ephesians 2:8.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8 clarifies that 'not of yourselves: it is the gift of God', indicating we are not saved by our own works.

questions.question: True or False: The text says we were children of mercy.
questions.explanation: The text does not state we were 'children of mercy', but rather 'children of wrath' as mentioned in Ephesians 2:3.

questions.question: True or False: The text says we were saved by our own faith alone.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8 states that we are saved 'by grace through faith', not by our own faith alone.

medium.title: Ephesians Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ephesians Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:9 say about salvation?
options: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
By grace are ye saved through faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:9 explicitly states that salvation is not based on works, emphasizing that no one can boast about their own efforts.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:10 promise will happen if someone follows the good works ordained by God?
options: They will walk in good works.
They will boast in their works.
questions.correctAnswer: They will walk in good works.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:10 affirms that we are created in Christ Jesus unto good works, indicating that following God's ordained works leads to walking in them.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:12, what were the Gentiles without?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:12 indicates that at that time, Gentiles were without Christ, aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to God's promises, leading to a state of having no hope and being without God.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:13 indicate about those who were once far off?
options: They were made nigh by the blood of Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: They were made nigh by the blood of Christ.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:13 states that those who were far off are brought near to God through the sacrifice of Christ's blood.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'middle wall of partition' mentioned in Ephesians 2:14?
options: It represents division between Jews and Gentiles.
It signifies the law of commandments.
It points to the hope of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: It represents division between Jews and Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:14 indicates that Christ broke down the middle wall of partition, symbolizing the removal of the division between Jews and Gentiles, creating unity.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:15, what did Christ abolish to make peace?
options: The law of commandments contained in ordinances.
questions.correctAnswer: The law of commandments contained in ordinances.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:15 states that Christ abolished the enmity and the law of commandments in order to create peace, uniting both groups into one new man.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:16 say about reconciliation?
options: Both are reconciled to God in one body by the cross.
Only the Jews are reconciled to God.
questions.correctAnswer: Both are reconciled to God in one body by the cross.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:16 explains that Christ reconciles both groups (Jews and Gentiles) to God in one body through His crucifixion.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:8 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: It is a gift of God, not of works.
It is only for the Jews.
questions.correctAnswer: It is a gift of God, not of works.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8 emphasizes that salvation is by grace through faith and is a gift from God, not something earned by works.

questions.question: In Ephesians 2:4, what does God’s mercy lead to?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4 highlights that God's rich mercy and great love lead to the quickening of those who were dead in sins, bringing them to life in Christ.

questions.question: What is the state of those who walk according to the course of this world, according to Ephesians 2:2?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:2 indicates that those who walk according to the course of this world are influenced by the spirit of disobedience, thus being children of disobedience.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:3, what is the nature of those who fulfill the desires of the flesh?
options: They are by nature children of wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: They are by nature children of wrath.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:3 explains that those who fulfill the desires of the flesh are naturally children of wrath, just like others who do not follow God.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:7, what does God show in the ages to come?
options: The exceeding riches of his grace.
The division between Jews and Gentiles.
questions.correctAnswer: The exceeding riches of his grace.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:7 states that God will show the exceeding riches of His grace in kindness towards us through Christ in the ages to come.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 2:5 states that we are saved by grace.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:5 clearly states that we are saved by grace, demonstrating the unearned favor of God.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 2:1 indicates that everyone is alive in trespasses and sins.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:1 states that we were dead in trespasses and sins, not alive, highlighting our need for salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 2:6 promises that we have been raised up and seated in heavenly places in Christ.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:6 confirms that we have been raised up and made to sit in heavenly places, not that we have not been raised.

hard.title: Ephesians Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ephesians Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who preached peace to those who were afar off and to those who were nigh?
questions.explanation: Jesus preached peace to those afar off and those nigh, as stated in Ephesians 2:17.

questions.question: What do both Gentiles and Jews have access to through the Spirit?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:18 states that through Him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 2:19, what are believers no longer considered?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:19 declares that believers are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints.

questions.question: What is the chief cornerstone of the foundation upon which believers are built?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:20 states that Jesus Christ himself is the chief corner stone of the foundation.

questions.question: What kind of temple are believers being built into according to Ephesians 2:21?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:21 indicates that the building grows into a holy temple in the Lord.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 2:22 say believers are built together for?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:22 states that believers are built together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'oikodome' in Ephesians 2:21 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Oikodome' in Ephesians 2:21 refers to the act of building or edification.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ephesians 2:14 where it states 'For he is our peace'?
questions.explanation: In Ephesians 2:14, calling Christ our peace is a metaphor illustrating His role in reconciliation.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of reconciliation found in Ephesians 2:16?
questions.explanation: Colossians 1:20 speaks of Christ reconciling all things to Himself, echoing the theme of reconciliation in Ephesians 2:16.

questions.question: Which passage from the Old Testament foreshadows the unity of Jews and Gentiles found in Ephesians 2:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:6 speaks of being a light to the Gentiles, foreshadowing the unity described in Ephesians 2:19.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Ephesians 2:17?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:16 precedes Ephesians 2:17, discussing reconciliation to God through the cross.

questions.question: What is the overarching theme of Ephesians 2:5-9 regarding salvation?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:5-9 emphasizes that salvation is by grace through faith, not of works.

questions.question: Ephesians 2:4 highlights God's character. What does it emphasize about Him?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4 highlights God's rich mercy, contrasting with the state of being dead in sins.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ephesians 2, believers are made alive together with Christ.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:5 states that God has quickened us together with Christ, affirming that believers are made alive.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 2 teaches that salvation is attainable through personal works.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:9 clarifies that salvation is not of works, lest any man should boast.

theological.title: Ephesians Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ephesians Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ephesians 2:1 teach about human sin?
options: Humans are spiritually dead due to trespasses and sins
Humans are inherently righteous despite sin
Sin has no effect on spiritual life
Humans are only physically dead because of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are spiritually dead due to trespasses and sins
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:1 states that we were 'dead in trespasses and sins,' teaching the doctrine of spiritual death as a result of sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about spiritual influence is taught in Ephesians 2:2?
options: Believers once walked according to the prince of the power of the air, a spirit influencing disobedience
The world has no influence on spiritual behavior
The prince of the power of the air is a metaphor for human government
Spiritual influence is irrelevant to human choices
questions.correctAnswer: Believers once walked according to the prince of the power of the air, a spirit influencing disobedience
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:2 describes how believers formerly walked according to worldly principles, influenced by the 'prince of the power of the air,' indicating satanic spiritual influence over disobedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about human nature does Ephesians 2:3 teach?
options: Humans are by nature children of wrath, fulfilling fleshly desires
Humans are naturally inclined towards holiness
Sinful desires are external and not innate
Humans are neutral in moral disposition
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are by nature children of wrath, fulfilling fleshly desires
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:3 teaches that by nature humans are 'children of wrath,' living according to fleshly lusts and desires, emphasizing inherent sinfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ephesians 2:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4 highlights that God is 'rich in mercy,' demonstrating His compassionate and forgiving nature despite human sinfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly shown in Ephesians 2:7?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:7 speaks of the 'exceeding riches of his grace,' emphasizing God's unmerited favor and kindness toward believers.

questions.question: How does Ephesians 2:10 connect to the broader biblical theme of sanctification?
options: It teaches believers are God’s workmanship created for good works prepared beforehand
It denies the need for good works in Christian life
It focuses only on justification without sanctification
It teaches salvation is earned by works
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches believers are God’s workmanship created for good works prepared beforehand
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:10 presents sanctification as God preparing believers for good works, integrating the theme of divine purpose and transformation in the Christian life.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ephesians 2:14 make concerning the unity of Jews and Gentiles?
options: Christ is our peace who broke down the dividing wall between Jew and Gentile
The law remains the barrier between Jews and Gentiles
Gentiles remain separate from God's people
Only Jews have access to God through Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is our peace who broke down the dividing wall between Jew and Gentile
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:14 illustrates the fulfillment of God's plan to unify Jews and Gentiles into one body through Christ, breaking down previous divisions.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ephesians 2:13 and 2:18 teach about access to God?
options: Believers are made near by Christ’s blood and have access to the Father through one Spirit
Access to God is only for the Jewish people
Believers must earn access through works
The Holy Spirit has no role in access to God
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are made near by Christ’s blood and have access to the Father through one Spirit
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:13 speaks of being made near by the blood of Christ, while 2:18 emphasizes access to the Father through the Spirit, together teaching reconciliation and access through Christ and the Spirit.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ephesians 2:15 and 2:16 teach about reconciliation?
options: Christ abolished enmity and reconciled both Jews and Gentiles to God in one body by the cross
The law remains a barrier to reconciliation
Reconciliation is only between individuals, not groups
questions.correctAnswer: Christ abolished enmity and reconciled both Jews and Gentiles to God in one body by the cross
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:15 explains how Christ abolished the law’s enmity to create one new man, and 2:16 describes reconciliation of both groups to God through the cross.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ephesians 2:19 and 2:20 teach about the church’s foundation and identity?
options: Believers are no longer strangers but fellow citizens built on the foundation of apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone
The church is built on human wisdom and traditions
Believers remain outsiders to God's household
The foundation of the church is the law
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are no longer strangers but fellow citizens built on the foundation of apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:19 states believers' new identity as fellow citizens in God’s household, while 2:20 identifies the church’s foundation as apostles and prophets with Christ as the chief cornerstone.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Ephesians 2:8-9 teaches that works have no role in the Christian life at all. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Salvation is by grace through faith and not by works to prevent boasting
Works are the basis of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by grace through faith and not by works to prevent boasting
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8-9 clearly teaches salvation is a gift of God by grace through faith, not of works, to exclude boasting; it does not deny the role of works in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ephesians 2:12 teach about the condition of Gentiles before Christ?
options: Gentiles were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and without hope or God
Gentiles were included in Israel’s covenants
Gentiles had equal access to God before Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and without hope or God
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:12 describes Gentiles as outsiders to Israel’s promises, without hope and without God, emphasizing their need for Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Ephesians 2:6?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:6 shows God’s sovereignty in raising believers and seating them in heavenly places with Christ, demonstrating divine authority and power.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from Ephesians 2:22 and 2:21 about the church?
options: Believers are built together into a holy temple as a habitation of God through the Spirit
The church is a physical building only
The Spirit has no role in the church’s unity
The church is not connected to God’s dwelling
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are built together into a holy temple as a habitation of God through the Spirit
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:21-22 teaches the church as a spiritually united temple where God dwells through His Spirit, emphasizing corporate holiness and divine indwelling.

questions.question: How does Ephesians 2:17 contribute to the biblical narrative arc of reconciliation?
options: Christ preached peace to both those afar off and those near, signifying universal reconciliation
Peace is only offered to the Jewish people
Reconciliation is limited to earthly rulers
Christ preached judgment rather than peace
questions.correctAnswer: Christ preached peace to both those afar off and those near, signifying universal reconciliation
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:17 highlights Christ’s mission to bring peace to all peoples, fulfilling the biblical theme of universal reconciliation through the gospel.
